cf.title: Fix UNIQUE WITHOUT OVERLAPS + NULLS NOT DISTINCT + multiranges

input.subject: Fix UNIQUE WITHOUT OVERLAPS + NULLS NOT DISTINCT + multiranges

verdict_reasoning: This is a correctness fix for a shipped feature: a declared NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraint accepts duplicates on multirange columns. No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is fixable: the backpatch gives 18 users no guidance for tables that already hold duplicate NULL keys. That point and the C signature change in a back branch are for a committer to judge.

brief.title: Fix unique without overlaps with nulls not distinct on multiranges
brief.problem: A unique or primary key constraint declared with WITHOUT OVERLAPS and NULLS NOT DISTINCT treats NULLs as distinct when the range column is a multirange, so it accepts duplicates. Ranges work because their GiST index is not lossy; multiranges go through index_recheck_constraint, which never treats nulls as matching. Andres Freund reported the bug.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a parameter to index_recheck_constraint that selects the null handling, so it behaves like check_exclusion_or_unique_constraint. Ordinary EXCLUDE constraints keep their current behaviour. The fix is to be backpatched through 18.
user_visible_surface: Changed behaviour: unique and primary key constraints using WITHOUT OVERLAPS and NULLS NOT DISTINCT on multirange columns now reject duplicate NULLs.
Changed C API: index_recheck_constraint in execIndexing.c gets a new parameter for null handling.
author_claims: Ranges already behave correctly; only lossy GiST cases such as multiranges are affected.
Ordinary EXCLUDE constraints are not affected, since they treat all operators as strict regardless of declaration.
EXCLUDE constraints with a non-strict operator such as IS NOT DISTINCT FROM accept two NULLs, and this assumption is documented only in a code comment.
SP-GiST could never support non-strict operators, because it never passes nulls to the opclass.
brief.thread_state: Osama Abdul Qader replied, restating the report and the open EXCLUDE question without new findings. Peter Eisentraut is listed as reviewer but has not posted; whether to allow, forbid or document non-strict operators in EXCLUDE constraints is open.
unclear: The material does not say whether existing tables on 18 may already hold duplicates that the fixed constraint would reject, or what users should do about them.
The patch does not say whether a release note or documentation change is planned for the behaviour change.
The thread does not say whether index_recheck_constraint is used by extensions, which matters for a C signature change in a backpatch.
The material does not show whether the regression tests cover both primary keys and unique constraints on multiranges.
search_queries: unique without overlaps nulls not distinct

objections.title: Backpatched fix gives no path for 18 tables already holding duplicates
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 18 has a multirange table with WITHOUT OVERLAPS and NULLS NOT DISTINCT, and it already holds duplicate NULL keys. After the minor update, a later REINDEX, or a pg_dump restore that rebuilds the constraint, may fail. The user first sees the duplicates during an upgrade or a restore.
objections.argument: The commit message says the bug "wrongly permitted duplicates", so some 18 tables can hold rows that the fixed constraint rejects. The patch touches only execIndexing.c and the regression tests, and it has no documentation hunk. The proposal does not say how users find such rows before or after updating. Backpatched constraint fixes usually come with a release-note query that finds violating rows and advice on whether to REINDEX.
objections.author_must_show: What release-note text and detection query will tell 18 users whether their multirange temporal keys already hold duplicate NULLs, and what to do about them?

critic.reasoning: The commit message says the bug "wrongly permitted duplicates", so 18 tables can hold rows that a rebuilt constraint rejects. The thread and the patch prose do not mention existing data, and the brief lists this as open.

refuted.title: No plan for multirange tables that already hold duplicate NULL keys
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 18.x has a multirange table with a WITHOUT OVERLAPS NULLS NOT DISTINCT key that already holds two rows with NULL key parts. After the minor update, restoring a dump of that table, or a later update that re-inserts an index entry, fails with a constraint violation. The user finds out during a restore or migration.
refuted.argument: The bug let invalid rows into tables, and the fix only changes enforcement for new index entries. The constraint stays marked valid on rows that break it, and a dump/restore rebuilds the index and runs the recheck, which now rejects them. The commit message (message #1) gives no release-note text, no query to find such rows, and no advice on fixing them. Backpatching through 18 means this hits users at a minor-version update, where they do not expect restores to fail.
refuted.author_must_show: What will the release note tell 18.x users about existing duplicate rows, and what query lets them find and fix those rows before they dump or restore?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The patch changes no on-disk format, so the pg_upgrade and safety framing adds nothing beyond the existing-duplicates point.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a parameter to index_recheck_constraint in execIndexing.c and is to be backpatched to 18.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Restoring a dump of an 18 table that already holds duplicate NULL keys may fail once the constraint is enforced.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message says "Backpatch-through: 18", and the fix changes constraint behaviour in a minor release.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What release-note text and detection query will tell 18 users whether their multirange temporal keys already hold duplicate NULLs, and how to repair them?
Is index_recheck_constraint visible to extensions, and if so, does the 18 backpatch keep the old signature working?
Do the new tests in without_overlaps.sql cover a multirange unique constraint with NULLS NOT DISTINCT for both the insert path and the update path?
Will the open question about non-strict operators in EXCLUDE constraints go to a separate thread, so that it does not hold up this fix?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut is signed up as reviewer in the CommitFest entry but has not posted in the thread. The owner needs to know the executor's exclusion-constraint recheck code and the temporal constraint feature.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in a minor release of 18: constraints start rejecting rows they accepted before. The owner also signs for the changed function signature in a back branch.
committability.author_follow_up: The author wrote the temporal constraint feature and offers in message #1 to send a separate patch for the EXCLUDE case.

priority.reason: The bug affects only unique constraints that combine WITHOUT OVERLAPS, NULLS NOT DISTINCT and a multirange column, but it lets a declared constraint accept duplicates. The patch is 8.4 KB and touches one executor file plus regression tests.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether index_recheck_constraint is exported, or whether the new parameter leaves ordinary EXCLUDE constraints unchanged as the commit message says.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant DISTINCT when GROUP BY already guarantees uniqueness
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Zsolt Parragi, Andres Taylor, David Rowley, Antonin Houska
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made the planner skip the DISTINCT step when a query has a plain GROUP BY (no GROUPING SETS), the clause is plain DISTINCT, and every GROUP BY key appears in the DISTINCT list. Each group yields one row, so the extra Sort and Unique nodes add no filtering.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers showed that v1 returned wrong results when the target list has a set-returning function, because SRF expansion happens after grouping but before DISTINCT. Reviewers also found that v1 matched keys by sort-group reference only and did not check opclass or collation. David Rowley judged the GROUP BY case too narrow and pointed to planner-wide UniqueKeys work instead. The author moved to the UniqueKeys patch series, then withdrew the entry after Antonin Houska pointed to newer and more complete unique-keys work posted elsewhere.
matched_queries: unique without overlaps nulls not distinct
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think only doing something just for that case is likely too narrow a scope.

precedents_retrieved.title: Erase the distinctClause if the result is unique by definition
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a list of UniqueKeys to RelOptInfo and tracks them through base relations, joins, subqueries, partitioned tables, unions, GROUP BY and DISTINCT. The planner uses the UniqueKeys to drop DISTINCT or GROUP BY when the result is already unique, and to extend join removal and semijoin reduction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The representation of UniqueKey was never settled. The patch stores a list of Expr, but reviewers wanted EquivalenceClasses. Ashutosh Bapat also found the patch larger than the feature was worth and objected to the special-casing of one-row relations. The entry sat in Waiting on Author, and the visible messages end in February 2021 with the author planning to split the work, with no reworked patch shown.
matched_queries: unique without overlaps nulls not distinct
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I agree that we should be storing them in EquivalenceClasses.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
Reverted commit(s): Revert structural changes to not-null constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
We added pg_constraint rows for all not-null constraints, first for
tables and later for domains; but while the ones for tables were
reverted, the ones for domains were not.  However, we did accidentally
revert ruleutils.c support for the ones on domains in 6f8bb7c1e961,
which breaks running pg_get_constraintdef() on them.  Put that back.

This is only needed in branch 17, because we've reinstated this code in
branch master with commit 14e87ffa5c54.  Add some new tests in both
branches.

I couldn't find anything else that needs de-reverting.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: fix NOT NULL constraint name comparison using makeObjectName
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves makeObjectName and pg_encoding_mbcliplen into src/common so that pg_dump can rebuild the server's truncated auto-generated NOT NULL constraint names. pg_dump would then match names longer than 63 bytes and omit the redundant CONSTRAINT clause for domains and table columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after finding that the claimed round-trip bug does not exist. pg_dump emits the name stored in pg_constraint, which the server has already truncated, so the restored constraint keeps the same name and only a redundant CONSTRAINT clause remains. The author judged that moving makeObjectName to src/common was too much work for that. No reviewer commented on the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So the decision is wrong, but the only consequence is that a name that could have been left out is written in a CONSTRAINT clause, which is functionally harmless, and the comment above determineNotNullFlags() already says as much.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch appears to need some work and has not been updated in several
weeks, so marking Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout
Reverted commit(s): Catalog NOT NULL constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit e056c557aef4 and minor later fixes thereof.

There's a few problems in this new feature -- most notably regarding
pg_upgrade behavior, but others as well.  This new feature is not in any
way critical on its own, so instead of scrambling to fix it we revert it
and try again in early 17 with these issues in mind.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove deprecated exclusive backup mode
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove the exclusive backup mode of pg_start_backup()/pg_stop_backup(), deprecated since 9.6, because a crash during an exclusive backup leaves a backup_label that can stop Postgres from restarting. Only non-exclusive backups, which need the session kept open from start to stop, would remain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch in July 2020, calling it a dead end, and said he would start a new thread with a new design. Early objections said two releases of deprecation was too short, and later ones said removal breaks users' backup scripts while the exclusive mode is not broken. The discussion then moved to a new mode that would let pg_stop_backup() run in a different session, and the author noted it still does not solve users writing backup_label into the data directory.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: None of this really solves the problem of what happens when the user dumps the backup_label into the data directory.

precedents_retrieved.title: SimpleLruTruncate() mutual exclusion (data loss from lack thereof)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch serializes SLRU truncation so that only one backend at a time runs vac_truncate_clog() and asyncQueueAdvanceTail() per cluster, and vac_update_datfrozenxid() per database. This closes a race in which two concurrent truncations can unlink a pg_xact segment that a backend has just recreated, which loses data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane questioned whether serialization fixes the race and wanted to keep concurrent truncation directory scans, and Noah Misch answered with a concrete event sequence. Dmitry Dolgov could not reproduce the bug with the posted script and measured only a small latency increase, and the thread ends there with no withdrawal message.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. Later versions drop the idea of holding pins on index pages: they add a table AM API (table_index_vischeck_tuples) so the index AM checks the visibility map while it still holds the page pin, and they also change nbtree to use it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message (v14, December 2025) only fixes a CFBot failure, and the entry was withdrawn about six months later with no visible objection or explanation. The author had moved a backpatchable version of the fix to a separate thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

roaster_notes.note: Neither listed precedent is the same idea or a close relative. [P1] reverted temporal keys over empty-range handling, a different defect, and that reason does not apply to this null-handling fix. [P18] fixed index-only scan rechecks and records an ABI concern in a different area; it does not count against this patch. The thread points to no earlier attempt at this fix, so no precedent was found.

The fix makes the behaviour match what NULLS NOT DISTINCT already promises, and ranges already behave this way, so it adds no new syntax and no GUC. The only compatibility gap from this angle is the missing guidance for existing data in a backpatch. The open question about non-strict EXCLUDE operators belongs to a separate patch.
The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL, catalog or wire protocol. The only persistent-state issue is data already admitted by the bug.

The fix tightens null handling in a constraint recheck for one constraint type. It adds no privilege, role, default, exposure path or code run by maintenance commands, and no unprivileged user gains any ability or information. Backpatching the C signature change is an ABI concern for another angle.

From the maintenance angle this is a small bugfix in one function, written by the author of the temporal constraint feature, and it leaves ordinary EXCLUDE constraints unchanged. Two points could not be checked without the code. First, whether index_recheck_constraint is exported, since a signature change in a backpatch would then need a compatibility wrapper. Second, how existing 18 tables that already hold duplicate NULLs are handled after a minor upgrade.

This is a correctness fix for a shipped feature, and no existing feature or extension gives the same result. Using a range column instead of a multirange avoids the bug but is not a fix. The patch extends the existing recheck function, so it adds no second mechanism and no new hook.

This is a correctness bug fix: a declared NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraint accepts duplicates on multirange columns, reported independently by Andres Freund (message #1). Demand is not the test for honouring a documented constraint, and the cost falls only on users of the feature.
